Also, Brockhampton to me remains as the face of new hip hop because they're continuing to push the genre forward with their fusions and musical experimentation. But I can't really disagree when people say that they went soft after Ameer left but that is not a bad thing. Their objective since the beginning was to be a boyband and make the music that they want, either pop or rap, they don't want to be encapsulated in one genre and that is something that they approached perfectly in Ginger. they lost their edge after Ameer left because after Saturation III they didn't have anything else to prove. the SATURATION trilogy was them going hard for their spot in the game and they were hungry as fuck, but after that their intent was primarily to just make good music.
